extracted.intended_audience: Users of ProQuest Regulatory Insight (researchers, librarians, policy analysts) who need to find public comments submitted to rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and product-imposed rules for locating and accessing public comments on proposed Federal Register rules within ProQuest Regulatory Insight, including supported search fields, archive behavior, and date coverage limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Comment Period (what comments are)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the Federal Register announcement of the Proposed Rule, there is text stating that 'Comments must be received on or before' a certain date. This is known as the Notice and Comment Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments included in Regulatory Insight are those submitted as part of the notice-and-comment process and posted on Regulations.gov; understand that 'comments' refers to submissions during that formal comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria / date coverage for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Insight includes comments posted from January 1, 2017 onward pertaining to Federal Register articles; it also includes retrospective comments relating to Dockets which were open for comment in 2016 and appear in Regulatory Histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a comment predates 1/1/2017 and is not part of a 2016 docket included in a Regulatory History, it will not be present in this product. Use this rule to set expectations about completeness and temporal coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments search form: permitted search fields
rubrics_metrics.description: You can access comments through the Comments search form where you can search by All Fields, Agency, Country, Organization, and Submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that full text is not an option on this form. Use metadata fields (Agency, Country, Organization, Submitter) or All Fields to locate comments when full-text searching is required elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier-based searching (Docket/RIN/Comment ID/Document Number)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can search for comments filed by Docket Number, RIN number, or Comment ID number. In addition, you can search by Document Number or RIN to return results for all individual comments as well as the Comments Archive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searching with specific identifiers (Docket, RIN, Comment ID, Document Number) is the most precise way to retrieve comment records or the full archive for a docket/RIN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search results behavior: individual comments vs Comments Archive
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results using All Fields, Agency, Country, Organization, Submitter or Comment ID Number will bring up individual comments. Using Document Number or RIN returns results for all individual comments as well as the Comments Archive (an archive of all comments for that RIN or docket number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose identifier searches when you want the archive context (all comments for a docket/RIN); use other metadata fields when seeking specific individual comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three access pathways to comments
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 3 ways to access Comments: (1) the Comments search form, (2) from within a Regulatory History (link to Comments Archive if RIN series has associated comments), and (3) from the Federal Register article (Proposed or Final Rules with comments will have links to the Comment Archive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one route fails, try another—e.g., find a related Regulatory History or the specific Federal Register article to reach the Comments Archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments Archive: metadata filters and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The top of the Comments Archive shows the filter where you can search the metadata (note the comments are not searchable), and filter by date or whether or not there are attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the archive filters to narrow by metadata, date range, or presence of attachments; remember you cannot full-text search the comment bodies within the archive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments Archive: Summary section contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary section of the Comments Archive gives you the RIN and Dockets, the title of the Proposed Rule, a link back to the Regulatory History and the public law text, and the URL for the Comments Archive you are viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Summary to confirm you are viewing the correct docket/RIN and to access the associated Regulatory History and source materials quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive ordering and navigation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The first item listed in the Comments section is the Proposed Rule so you can easily download it to consult when reading comments. You can sort the comments by ID number or by date (oldest/newest first). After the Federal Register Proposed Rule the comments will appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by downloading the Proposed Rule (first item) to understand context before reading comments; use sorting (ID or date) to control chronology or correspondence order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record provenance: comments reflect submitted content
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that the information provided here is based on what was filed when the comment was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that metadata and attachments mirror original submissions; verify Publication Details or related materials to see the exact content filed at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to view an individual comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the Publication Details or other materials as appropriate to view the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Publication Details link for each comment record to access attachments or the full comment package as available in the archive.
